name: Goshen First Fridays: Fire & Ice
what: Downtown Goshen opens the year with live ice carving, fire performers, an ice throne and sleigh for photos, and outdoor fires with free marshmallows. The Goshen Historical Museum stays open into the evening.
history: Downtown Goshen has held monthly First Fridays festivals since 2007.

name: Shipshewana Ice Festival & Chili Cook-Off
what: Professional carvers fill the town with ice sculptures, with live carving and a carving competition, plus a wing contest on Friday evening and a chili contest on Saturday.

name: St. Joseph Ice Fest
when: A weekend in late January / early February
what: Downtown St. Joseph fills with ice carvers working through the weekend, a lit 'Fire & Ice' tower, frozen games for families and a scavenger hunt along State and Pleasant streets.

name: Dowagiac Ice Time Festival
when: First Saturday of February (approx.), 10 am–4 pm
what: A one-day winter festival downtown with ice sculptures, a chili crawl through local restaurants, children's crafts, open shops and a fire-department s'mores tent.
history: The 2023 festival was the 26th annual, organized by the Greater Dowagiac Chamber of Commerce.

name: South Haven Ice Breaker Festival
what: More than forty ice sculptures line downtown South Haven, alongside cardboard sled races, horse-drawn wagon rides, outdoor skating and a chili cook-off.
history: 2027 is billed as the 33rd annual Ice Breaker.

name: Candlelight Christmas Parade
what: Dowagiac's evening holiday parade brings well over a hundred lighted units down Front Street, with a tree lighting at Beckwith Park, as part of the town's 'Celebrate the Holidays' season.
history: The 2019 parade was described as the 38th annual.

name: Santa's Candy Cane Express at Hesston Steam Museum
what: The steam museum's Christmas trains carry families through the snowy woods to visit Santa on two December weekends.

name: Christmas at Copshaholm
what: The History Museum decorates the Oliver family's 38-room Copshaholm mansion with Christmas trees on all three floors and themed table settings, and opens it for self-guided holiday tours.

name: Shipshewana Lights of Joy
what: A drive-through light show at the Shipshewana Trading Place: nearly two miles of lighted scenes with Christmas music on the car radio.

name: Sturgis Tree Lighting & Parade of Lights
when: First Thursday (tree lighting) and Friday (parade) of December
what: Sturgis lights its community tree with a children's reading of a Christmas poem, and the next evening more than fifty lighted floats from local businesses and clubs roll downtown.

name: Kalamazoo Nature Center Maple Sugar Festival
when: Early March, one Sunday, 9 am–4 pm
what: A day in the sugarbush at the Nature Center, with a pancake breakfast served with Michigan maple syrup and horse-drawn wagon rides around the grounds.
history: 2027 is billed as the 61st annual festival; it began as 'a kettle on a tripod.'

name: Sugar Camp Days at Bendix Woods
what: St. Joseph County Parks opens its sugar bush and sugar house for tours of sap gathering and boiling, with a Lions Club pancake breakfast, historical crafters, wagon rides and maple treats.
history: Bendix Woods was once part of the Studebaker proving-ground complex; its clubhouse and the CCC-planted 'Studebaker' pine-tree sign (1930s) are on the National Register.

name: Kalamazoo Living History Show
what: A large juried show for reenactors and history buffs, where makers sell pre-1890 clothing, gear and crafts at the county Expo Center; open to the public, with a different reenactment group hosting each year.
history: Founded 1976.

name: Wakarusa Maple Syrup Festival
when: Last full weekend of April, Friday–Sunday
what: A three-day small-town festival with a Saturday parade, carnival rides, dozens of vendor booths and plenty of maple treats.

name: Bonneyville Mill season
what: Elkhart County Parks' grist mill, billed as Indiana's oldest operating grist mill, grinds grain and sells its flour through the warm months; the park adds schoolhouse open houses, a Feature Grain Day and autumn leaf walks.

name: Blossomtime Festival
when: Late April to early May, ending with the Saturday Grand Floral Parade
what: Southwest Michigan's spring festival honoring the fruit-growing country, shared by some two dozen communities, with the Blessing of the Blossoms and a Grand Floral Parade that crosses the river from St. Joseph into Benton Harbor.
history: Established 1906 and described as Michigan's oldest multi-community festival; the Blessing of the Blossoms began in 1906 with Rev. W. J. Cady.

name: Dogwood Fine Arts Festival
what: Dowagiac's spring arts festival brings readings by visiting authors, concerts, art shows and a downtown art walk, and has commissioned public sculpture for the city.
history: Began in 1995, pairing visiting sculptors with local donors who commissioned public art (City of Dowagiac).

name: Shipshewana Flea Market season
when: Early May to late September, Tuesdays & Wednesdays
what: The Trading Place's big open-air flea market runs two days a week all summer, alongside the weekly antique and livestock auctions in the auction barn.

name: Hesston Steam Museum operating season
when: Weekends, Memorial Day through Labor Day
what: The La Porte County Historical Steam Society runs its steam and diesel railroads and antique machinery on summer weekends, opening with National Train Day and Memorial Day weekend.
history: First show and reunion held in 1957; the steam society was chartered as a nonprofit in 1968.

name: Quilt Gardens along the Heritage Trail
town: Elkhart County towns (Goshen, Nappanee, Middlebury, Elkhart and others)
what: Seventeen giant flower gardens planted in traditional quilt patterns across Elkhart County, free to tour along the Heritage Trail through the summer.
history: 2026 is the program's 19th year.

name: Three Oaks Flag Day Celebration
what: Billed as the world's largest Flag Day parade, Three Oaks turns out for a weekend of patriotic celebration honoring veterans and the flag.
history: First parade June 14, 1953, organized by Herb Flick under American Legion Post 204; it grew to a three-day celebration in the late 1970s.

name: Vicksburg Old Car Festival
what: More than a thousand old cars, from Model Ts to hot rods, fill the village on Saturday, while the Vicksburg Historic Village opens its buildings and an antique tractor and gas-engine show runs on the grounds.

name: Elkhart Jazz Festival
what: Four days of jazz in venues all over downtown Elkhart, including the historic Lerner Theatre, outdoor stages and small listening rooms.
history: Founded 1988.

name: Three Rivers Water Festival
what: Three days downtown and at Scidmore Park: an opening parade, arts and crafts, a soap box derby, car show, duck race and fireworks over the rivers.
history: The 2019 festival was the 63rd annual (City of Three Rivers).

name: Civil War Train Raids at Hesston
what: A living-history weekend at the Hesston Steam Museum, with Civil War reenactors staging train raids on the museum's railroad.

name: St. Joseph County 4-H Fair
what: The county's 4-H fair at the Ironwood Road fairgrounds, with livestock and open-class exhibits, a queen pageant, youth talent contest, parades and rides.

name: Krasl Art Fair on the Bluff
what: A juried outdoor art fair spread through Lake Bluff Park above Lake Michigan, run by the Krasl Art Center.

name: LaGrange County 4-H Fair
what: A week of 4-H exhibits and livestock with grandstand rodeo, truck and tractor pulls, harness racing by the local Trottingbred association, and Friday fireworks.

name: LaPorte County Fair
what: Billed as Indiana's oldest county fair, with livestock and open-class shows, rodeo and grandstand events, and Pioneerland, a living-history village of early Indiana pioneer life.
history: Established 1845; Pioneerland added in 1995.

name: Van Buren Youth Fair
what: Van Buren County's youth and 4-H fair at the Hartford fairgrounds, with livestock shows, exhibits and grandstand events.

name: Elkhart County 4-H Fair
what: One of Indiana's largest ticketed events, drawing about 200,000 people for nine days of 4-H livestock and exhibits, grandstand shows, a famous food row and the Heritage Park stage.

name: Blueberry u-pick season
when: July through August (some varieties into mid-September)
what: South Haven sits at the heart of Michigan's blueberry country, and through July and August farms and u-pick fields around town open for picking.
history: The area claims the world's largest concentration of blueberry growers, nearly 300 farmers within 50 miles.

name: Coloma Glad-Peach Festival
when: Late July / first days of August
what: Coloma's summer festival celebrates the area's peaches and gladiolus with a parade, carnival, walk/run and evening events downtown.

name: Fort St. Joseph Archaeology Open House
what: Each August the archaeologists excavating the site of the 18th-century French colonial fort on the St. Joseph River open their dig to the public, with artifact displays, 'ask an archaeologist' tables, guided tours and a living history village of costumed reenactors.
history: Western Michigan University's Fort St. Joseph Archaeological Project has more than 25 years of research at the site.

name: Cass County Fair
what: Cass County's agricultural fair, with livestock shows, still exhibits and a youth auction, a carnival, and grandstand rodeos, tractor pulls and demolition derbies.
history: Held since 1851; 2026 marked 175 years.

name: Kalamazoo County Fair
what: Five days of 4-H livestock and animal shows, a petting farm, stage shows and a Saturday-night rodeo at the county Expo Center grounds on Lake Street.

name: Abbott's Magic Get-Together
what: Magicians from around the world gather in the little village of Colon, home of Abbott's Magic Company, for four days of lectures, competitions and public evening shows.
history: Since 1934, founded by Percy Abbott and Recil Bordner.

name: National Blueberry Festival
when: Second weekend of August (approx.), four days
what: South Haven's long-running harvest festival honors the area's blueberry growers with four days of summer celebration by the lake.
history: Described as one of the longest-running fruit festivals in the nation; 2026 was billed as the 64th annual (https://www.southhaven.org/events/the-64th-annual-national-blueberry-festival/).

name: Berrien County Youth Fair
what: Berrien County's youth fair, with livestock and youth exhibits, fair royalty, a large-animal auction, tractor pulls, bull riding and a demolition derby.

name: Hesston Labor Day Weekend Steam & Power Show
what: The steam museum's biggest weekend: steam engines, antique machinery and trains in action, with a steam-powered threshing machine working the harvest.
history: The first show and reunion was held in 1957.

name: Michigan Flywheelers Antique Engine & Tractor Show
what: The museum's biggest show fills its 80-acre grounds with hundreds of working antique engines and tractors, a sawmill and shingle mill, a 1920s-style 'Olde Town' and a small railroad.

name: Paw Paw Wine & Harvest Festival
what: Paw Paw celebrates the grape harvest in the heart of Michigan wine country with family events, wine tasting, a parade and a 5K.

name: Nappanee Apple Festival
what: Opens by cutting a giant baked apple pie, then four days of parade, three stages, more than 150 exhibitors and apple fritters, dumplings and cider.

name: La Porte Sunflower Fair
what: A downtown community fair along Michigan Avenue with craft and nonprofit vendors, a farmers market, a rib cook-off, a car show and a sunflower-growing contest.

name: St. Joseph County Grange Fair
what: Michigan's Grange fair keeps the county fair tradition late in the season, with grandstand events, a community stage and daily free events at the Centreville fairgrounds.

name: Michiana Mennonite Relief Sale
what: A Mennonite community tradition at the Elkhart County fairgrounds: food booths, a live quilt auction and other sales, all raising money for Mennonite Central Committee relief work.
history: First sale held in 1968.

name: Vicksburg Harvest Festival
when: Last Sunday of September, 11 am–4 pm
what: The Vicksburg Historical Society opens its Historic Village, general store, print shop and schoolhouse for a free day of crafts and fiber demonstrations, antique tractors, wagon rides and pumpkin decorating, celebrating the area's farm heritage.
history: The 2024 festival was the 14th annual.

name: Apple Cider Century
what: A one-day bicycle tour from Three Oaks through orchard and wine country, with routes from 15 to 100 miles and cider and fruit along the way.
history: Started 1974; organized by the Three Oaks Spokes Bicycle Club.

name: Apple-picking season in the Fruit Belt
town: Coloma, Berrien Springs, Galien, Three Oaks and other towns
what: Berrien County's orchards open for u-pick apples from mid-August into October, many with farm markets, cider and wagon rides.
history: Jollay Orchards in Coloma dates its farm to 1857.

name: Giant Straw Bale Art Trail
what: A free self-guided autumn trail of giant round straw bales turned into colorful characters and scenes by local artists and businesses across four towns.

name: Under the Harvest Moon Festival
when: A Saturday in mid-October, 10 am–4 pm
what: Dowagiac's autumn festival brings vintage tractors, an open-air antique market, fall produce, Michigan-made crafts, blacksmith demonstrations and a scarecrow contest downtown.

name: Fall colour in Southwest Michigan
when: Peak usually the first two weeks of October
town: St. Joseph, Coloma, Berrien Springs, Niles, South Haven and the Red Arrow Highway
what: The orchard and dune country turns in early October; the tourism council suggests drives along Red Arrow Highway and Blue Star Highway, vineyard roads near Baroda, and the trails at Fernwood Botanical Garden in Niles.

name: Maple Hill Holiday Parade
when: A Saturday in late November, 11 am
what: Kalamazoo's downtown holiday parade of marching bands, giant balloons and floats, with shops on the Kalamazoo Mall opening the holiday season.
history: Founded in 1962 by the Gilmore Brothers department store.
Organized by Cassopolis Main Street, the village’s downtown organization.
name: Stone Lake Ice Fishing Bowl
when: A Saturday in January, when the ice is at least six inches thick; lines in at 6 am, fish measured by 11 am
what: A hook-and-line contest for the longest bluegill, crappie and perch through the ice of Stone Lake, with check-in at the beach Snack Shack near 203 S. Disbrow and awards afterward on Broadway. Entry is $30 cash; the 2026 bowl was postponed for thin ice, so watch for the new date.

history: Organized by Cassopolis Main Street, the village’s downtown organization.
name: Beach Bash
when: First weekend of June, Friday and Saturday
what: Two days on Broadway and at Stone Lake Beach: food trucks, a beer garden, a vendor market, a kids’ area and foam party, live music each night, fireworks on Friday and a drone show on Saturday.

history: Organized by Cassopolis Main Street, the village’s downtown organization.
name: Lakeside Live
when: Thursday evenings, June to August, 6–9 pm
what: A different band every Thursday night on the beach at Stone Lake, all summer long. Bring a blanket and a friend.

history: Organized by Cassopolis Main Street, the village’s downtown organization.
name: Beach Blankets & Blockbusters
when: Friday evenings, June to early September, films at 7 pm
what: Family movie nights on the sand at Stone Lake Beach, with popcorn from the Snack Shack and the odd double feature.

history: Organized by Cassopolis Main Street, the village’s downtown organization.
name: Rock the Block
when: A Saturday in July and one in August, 7–10 pm
what: Downtown Cassopolis’s summer concert series: two Saturday nights of live bands, with food vendors.

history: Organized by Cassopolis Main Street, the village’s downtown organization.
name: Christmas in Cassopolis
when: First Saturday of December, late afternoon into the evening
what: Santa and crafts at the Marketplace on Broadway, cookies and cocoa at the VFW, an elf scavenger hunt that starts at the 1899 courthouse, caroling down Broadway at 6, and the tree lit under the arches at Stone Lake Beach just after. Broadway is closed to traffic from York to Water Street.
